prompt_text:
The figure summarizes how the NLRP3 inflammasome is triggered through a two-step process. On the left, a “priming” signal from microbial or inflammatory cues such as LPS, TNF, or IL-1 activates receptors and downstream NF-κB signaling. This induces transcription of inflammasome-related components, including NLRP3 and the cytokine precursors pro–IL-1β and pro–IL-18, setting the cell up for activation.

The larger right side shows the “activation” phase, where many different danger signals converge on NLRP3. These include ATP acting through P2X7, pore-forming toxins, RNA viruses, particulate matter and crystals, and intracellular stress signals from mitochondria, lysosomes, and the Golgi. A recurring theme is ion imbalance, especially K+ efflux, along with Ca2+ flux, chloride movement, cathepsin release from damaged lysosomes, mitochondrial ROS, oxidized mitochondrial DNA, and metabolic changes involving hexokinase. Although the upstream triggers differ, they appear to funnel into NLRP3 oligomerization with ASC and caspase-1 to form the inflammasome.

Once assembled, caspase-1 processes pro–IL-1β and pro–IL-18 into active cytokines and cleaves gasdermin D, whose membrane pores drive inflammatory cytokine release and pyroptotic cell death.
